_role: Labelled routing cases for the Sovereign System One evaluator (SSO contract §8.5) and for backend-vs-backend parity between TypeSafe Jev and the local laya façade. Consumed by system-one-eval (Rust) and by tests/system-one/routing-corpus.test.mjs (JS validation). Schema and honest limitations: tests/system-one/README.md.

_schema.prompt: A user turn, as a user would actually type it. Always >= 24 chars so the router's min_prompt_chars skip never fires on a case.
_schema.expected_skill: A directory name under the skills tree that survives loadCandidates(), or the literal "none".
_schema.rationale: Why that label and not the nearest wrong one. A label without a stated reason is an opinion.
_schema.late_discriminative: true when the expected skill's rubric is longer than 48 tokens AND its first when-to-use / when-NOT-to-use boundary clause begins after the 48-token cut, so laya's unconditional per-option truncation (SSO contract §10.1) would amputate the clause that makes the label correct. Computed, not judged: 48 tokens taken as 192 chars from the estate's own datum (median 461-char description ≈ 115 tokens), first boundary clause located by the marker regex recorded in tests/system-one/README.md. An estimate of a cut, not a tokenisation of it — the façade reports the real compressed token count in sso.shortlisted. system-one-eval reports this subgroup separately; it is never excluded from the headline number.

_provenance.items-json-tier-A: Verbatim from skills/system-one/scripts/items.json tier A — prompts authored in earlier sessions, before this corpus and by a different task. The only genuinely independent prompts here.
_provenance.directory-derived: Written from the 'When to Choose' / 'NOT for' columns of skills/SKILL-DIRECTORY.md, which is authored separately from the frontmatter `description` the router actually scores. Independent of the text under test, but not of this repo.
_provenance.log-shaped: Conversational turns written to match the SHAPE of the 66 `none` picks and 13 short-prompt skips in ~/.claude/skill-route.jsonl. The log records outcomes, never prompt text, so nothing here is a recovered user turn.

cases.prompt: Break this epic into vertical-slice issues and put them on the project board for next sprint.
cases.rationale: Issue decomposition and project boards are github-project-management; PR review would be github-code-review.

cases.prompt: Set up pre-task and post-task hooks so agents hand off session state and format files automatically.
cases.rationale: Persistent pre/post task hooks and session handoffs are hooks-automation; a one-off swarm would be swarm-advanced.

cases.prompt: The Vite server on my host machine won't load in the sidecar Chrome because of CORS, and the camera API needs https.
cases.rationale: CORS and secure-context failures reaching a host dev server are the HTTPS-bridge job; general page driving would be browser.

cases.prompt: Drop six crates onto the conveyor with real gravity and contacts, and hand the trajectories to the animation.
cases.rationale: Gravity and contact dynamics producing trajectories for Blender is isaac-sim; a robot description file would be cad-robot.

cases.prompt: Build an analysis notebook that loads the sales CSV, runs every cell and exports the result to HTML.
cases.rationale: Authoring and executing a .ipynb and exporting it is jupyter-notebooks; a stateful kernel loop with no notebook would be codeact.

cases.prompt: Pick up where we left off yesterday: rebuild the context from git and my plan, and tell me which phase we're in.
cases.rationale: Session context hydration and phased plan tracking is lazy-fetch's row.

cases.prompt: Find recruiters at Graphcore on LI and draft a short connection note to the two most relevant.
cases.rationale: Profile search and messaging on LinkedIn is the linkedin row; generic scraping would be scrapling.

cases.prompt: Port our Three.js product viewer to the Quest 3 with passthrough and hand tracking.
cases.rationale: Quest WebXR with passthrough and hand tracking is meta-xr-sdk; plain 3D rendering is excluded by it.

cases.prompt: Make a fifteen-second kinetic type piece about latency, cut to a music track.
cases.rationale: Kinetic type film cut to music with no narration or footage is motion-designer; a narrated video from an idea would be open-montage.

cases.prompt: This API answers 402 Payment Required with an L402 challenge. Wire the call so it pays within a capped budget and retries.
cases.rationale: A 402 challenge on a metered API with capped spend is payment-router's row.

cases.prompt: Our eight-agent swarm has slowed to a crawl. Find which agent or channel is the bottleneck.
cases.rationale: Profiling a slow Claude Flow swarm is performance-analysis; GPU kernel profiling would be cuda.

cases.prompt: The weekly podcast job landed nothing in the evidence ledger this week. Debug the cron and promote what's waiting.
cases.rationale: The standing weekly pipeline and ledger promotion are podcast-knowledge-ingest; a backfill would be podcast-bulk-ingest.

cases.prompt: I've finished the market analysis doc. Add a sidecar that lists each source, whether it was verified, and how confident we are.
cases.rationale: A post-hoc sidecar of sources and confidence on finished research is provenance-tracking; live citation checking would be web-researcher.

cases.prompt: What are people on r/homelab saying about the new mini PCs this month? Pull the top threads and comments.
cases.rationale: Subreddit browsing and thread retrieval is the reddit row.

cases.prompt: Design how our assistant app remembers users across sessions and earns more autonomy over time, with controls to forget.
cases.rationale: Persistent memory, graduated trust and forgetting controls are relationship-design's stated scope.

cases.prompt: Produce a typeset white paper on UK water-sector challenges with data charts, a bibliography and a Wardley map.
cases.rationale: A researched LaTeX white paper with charts and citations is report-builder; compiling an existing .tex would be latex-documents.

cases.prompt: We're on pgvector and an external embeddings API. What in the RuVector stack could replace them, and what do we delete?
cases.rationale: Migration from aging tech to a RuVector replacement is ruvector-catalog's row; how a RuvNet repo behaves internally would be ruvnet-brain.

cases.prompt: How does ruflo actually decide swarm topology? Check the source rather than guessing from memory.
cases.rationale: How a RuvNet tool works, grounded in its indexed source, is ruvnet-brain; choosing a capability would be ruvector-catalog.

cases.prompt: Before we take this system over from the other team, give me a pre-mortem from its diagram corpus: what would worry an outsider?
cases.rationale: A pre-mortem from an existing diagrams corpus before a takeover is sealmap-review; writing the corpus would be diagrams-as-code.

cases.prompt: Embed the trained warehouse splat in our Three.js page with clickable annotations linked to the asset records.
cases.rationale: A splat inside a Three.js scene with annotations is spark-scene; cleaning the splat would be supersplat.

cases.prompt: Is the difference in satisfaction scores between the two groups significant? The data is an SPSS .sav file.
cases.rationale: A significance test on an SPSS .sav is statcraft's row; a notebook would be jupyter-notebooks.

cases.prompt: Chain three agents so the extractor's output feeds the transformer and that feeds the validator.
cases.rationale: Each step's output feeding the next is stream-chain; parallel agents would be swarm-advanced.

cases.prompt: Open this trained .ply splat, delete the floaters round the edge, and compress it to SOG for the web.
cases.rationale: Inspecting, cleaning and compressing a finished splat is supersplat; training would be lichtfeld-studio.

cases.prompt: Make a playable Minecraft world of central York from the real streets and buildings.
cases.rationale: A Minecraft world from real geography is terracraft; a fictional game world would be game-dev.

cases.prompt: Fix the straight quotes, double hyphens and line length in the React components that render the article body.
cases.rationale: Typographic detail in UI code that renders text is typography; a broader visual audit would be design-audit.

cases.prompt: In my running UE5 editor, spawn twenty street lights along the spline and start a PIE session.
cases.rationale: Direct UE5 editor control and PIE sessions are unreal-engine; design-level game work would be game-dev.

cases.prompt: Be honest: is event sourcing plus Kafka for a ten-user internal tool just there to look impressive?
cases.rationale: Complexity built to impress rather than ship is vanity-engineering-review's whole remit.

cases.prompt: Check that the fixes the changelog claims are still present in the tree against the signed witness manifest.
cases.rationale: Verifying shipped fixes against the witness manifest is verification-quality's stated scope.

cases.prompt: Produce a stop-motion short with the same clay character in every shot, versioned revisions and acceptance checks.
cases.rationale: Continuity held across shots with acceptance gates is video-production; a montage from an idea would be open-montage.

cases.prompt: This date-range parser has now worked in four projects. Save it as a verified reusable helper with its assertions.
cases.rationale: Persisting a proven general-purpose function with assertions is voyager; storing an IF/THEN lesson would be expel-lesson-extractor.

cases.prompt: The canvas animation computes a Voronoi diagram every frame and JavaScript can't keep up. Move the geometry to WebAssembly.
cases.rationale: Performance-critical web graphics with a WASM maths backend is wasm-js; non-graphical WASM would be rust-development.

cases.prompt: Archive every talk on this conference's YouTube channel as markdown transcripts with the links they mention.
cases.rationale: Batch channel transcripts as standalone notes is the archiver; feeding them into the ontology would be podcast-bulk-ingest.

cases.prompt: I only need the gist of this one docs page, no clicking around. Here's the URL.
cases.rationale: Sounds like browser work, but one page summarised without interaction is web-summary; browser is for live interaction.

cases.prompt: Run an overnight experiment loop on our bundle size: change the build config, measure, keep the wins.
cases.rationale: Contains 'experiment' and 'research'-adjacent wording but is metric optimisation, not web research (deep-research).

cases.prompt: Find me two or three recent articles on Rust async cancellation and give me the raw page text to work from.
cases.rationale: Sounds like a research brief, but it asks for raw extracts from a quick keyword search; deep-research would be overkill.

cases.prompt: Draw the retry flow as a quick .mmd file I can commit next to the handler code.
cases.rationale: Sounds like the diagrams corpus by wording, but one committed .mmd is mermaid-diagrams, not diagrams-as-code.

cases.prompt: I need a polished, on-brand architecture diagram for the investor deck, matching our website colours.
cases.rationale: Sounds like an architecture diagram set, but one branded published visual is diagram-design, not diagrams-as-code or mermaid-diagrams.

cases.prompt: Render a product image of this STEP file for the landing page.
cases.rationale: Sounds like Blender rendering, but a photoreal still of a CAD model is cad-render.

cases.prompt: Model a low-poly fantasy cottage I can drop into my game as an asset.
cases.rationale: Sounds like game development, but authoring one 3D mesh asset is blender; game-dev is the multi-system studio.

cases.prompt: Can the 3 mm walls on this enclosure actually be injection moulded, or do I need to change them?
cases.rationale: Sounds like a strength question, but manufacturability is cad's check; cad-fea is load and deflection.

cases.prompt: Simulate the arm toppling under gravity when the base joint fails, and give me the trajectory.
cases.rationale: Sounds like the robot description skill, but running dynamics is isaac-sim; cad-robot only writes URDF/MJCF.

cases.prompt: Animate how a token bucket rate limiter refills and drains, precise enough for a lecture.
cases.rationale: Sounds like motion graphics, but an animation that teaches a mechanism is manim, not motion-designer.

cases.prompt: Fix the undefined control sequence error in chapter3.tex so the thesis compiles again.
cases.rationale: Sounds like the book pipeline, but fixing compilation of an existing .tex is latex-documents.

cases.prompt: Agents should each take a module of the migration in parallel, with the coordinator reassigning work if one dies.
cases.rationale: Sounds like hive-mind, but there is no voting or consensus: parallel streams with fault tolerance is swarm-advanced.

cases.prompt: Generate the specs, domain model, ADRs and task plan in one go from the requirements doc I just attached.
cases.rationale: Sounds like bhil's artefact chain, but a one-shot documentation set from a PRD is prd2build.

cases.prompt: My RwSignal panics with 'signal disposed' when I navigate away from the route in a view! component. Why?
cases.rationale: Sounds like general Rust debugging, but a Leptos reactivity panic is leptos, not rust-development.

cases.prompt: Make our marketing page show up in Search Console for the right keywords and fix the meta tags.
cases.rationale: Sounds like AI-search optimisation, but Search Console, keywords and meta tags are classic SEO: toprank, not bencium-aeo.

cases.prompt: Before we lock the brand, which chart types suit a dense finance dashboard on a phone screen?
cases.rationale: Sounds like a dashboard build (open-design), but looking up a chart type before a brand exists is the reference database.

cases.prompt: Turn my phone video of the garden into a dataset and train a splat from it.
cases.rationale: Sounds like cleanup in the browser editor (supersplat) or dataset generation (comfyui), but video-to-COLMAP plus training is lichtfeld-studio.

cases.prompt: As an outside review, not a rewrite: does the auth topic in the diagrams corpus still match the code it cites, and what would worry you?
cases.rationale: Sounds like re-verifying the corpus (diagrams-as-code), but a review-only check of a topic against cited code, with no re-stamping, is sealmap-review's inline mode.

cases.prompt: Release 2.4 needs a changelog, a version bump across the monorepo packages and a rollback plan.
cases.rationale: Sounds like multi-repo coordination, but a monorepo release is github-release-management; github-multi-repo is cross-repo sync.

cases.prompt: Ask OpenAI's coding agent to take over this failing migration; I'm stuck and want it rescued.
cases.rationale: Sounds like a reasoning consult, but rescue by delegation to OpenAI is codex-companion, not deepseek-reasoning.

cases.prompt: Which RuVector crate gives me hybrid search with metadata filters, and how do I reach it from npm?
cases.rationale: Sounds like a source question for ruvnet-brain, but finding a capability and its access path is ruvector-catalog.

cases.prompt: Our swarm keeps timing out; is the mesh topology the problem, and what concurrency should we use?
cases.rationale: Sounds like swarm setup, but tuning topology and concurrency on a slow swarm is performance-analysis.

cases.prompt: Harden the login API against injection and check the session tokens can't be forged.
cases.rationale: Sounds like host hardening, but this is application/API security: security-testing, not defense-security.

cases.prompt: Work through this data step by step in a live Python session: load it, run a t-test, and keep the dataframe so the next step can depend on the result.
cases.rationale: Sounds like statcraft by its t-test, but state persisting across steps with results driving the next step is codeact; no SPSS syntax or .sav is involved.

cases.prompt: Search this small service for every place we read the DATABASE_URL variable.
cases.rationale: Sounds like code intelligence or web search, but a grep over a small project needs no skill; codebase-memory is for 500+ file repos.

cases.prompt: Remember that I prefer UK spelling in everything you write for me.
cases.rationale: Sounds like a memory skill, but storing one preference is a direct memory call; no listed skill owns it.

cases.prompt: Is a sequence diagram or a flowchart better for showing retry logic, generally speaking?
cases.rationale: Mentions diagrams but asks for an opinion, not a diagram; drawing nothing means no diagram skill.

cases.prompt: Set a reminder for me to ring the dentist tomorrow morning.
cases.rationale: Sounds like a scheduler, but a personal reminder is not a recurring agent task (hermes-scheduler) and no skill owns calendars.

cases.prompt: Add a short section to the README explaining how to run the tests locally.
cases.rationale: Sounds like an explainer or docs audit, but a single README edit is excluded by both explainer and docs-alignment.

cases.prompt: Fix the typo in the error message on line 40 of main.rs, nothing else.
cases.rationale: Mentions Rust, but a one-word edit needs no toolchain or workflow skill.

cases.prompt: What's the difference between a mutex and a semaphore? A short answer is fine.
cases.rationale: A conceptual question; no reasoning consult (deepseek-reasoning) is warranted for a textbook answer.

cases.prompt: Resize the PR description so it fits GitHub's character limit and tidy the wording.
cases.rationale: Mentions GitHub and PRs but is a plain text edit, not review, release or workflow work.

cases.prompt: Which of these two headlines reads better for the launch email? Just pick one.
cases.rationale: Sounds like writing help, but choosing between two lines needs no de-slop or design skill.

cases.prompt: Explain the output of that benchmark run in plain terms, I just want to understand the numbers.
cases.rationale: Mentions a benchmark, but interpreting one run is not an optimisation loop (autoresearch) or profiling skill.

cases.prompt: Rename the variable `cfg` to `config` throughout this one function and keep the behaviour identical.
cases.rationale: A single-function rename is ordinary editing; no skill adds anything and a pick would only cost context.

cases.prompt: Can you explain what this regular expression matches? ^(?:[a-z0-9-]+\.)+[a-z]{2,}$
cases.rationale: Reading one regex back in prose is a direct answer, not a skill's workflow.

cases.prompt: Bump the timeout in the retry loop from 5 to 10 seconds and update the comment above it.
cases.rationale: A two-line constant change needs no skill; picking one is the false-positive cost the none label measures.
